kill_test: synthetic floor negligible at n~30 OR estimator disagreement < own bias
primary_metric: std(Hhat) vs window/estimator/freq; cross-estimator MAD vs floor
result_summary: Intraday H poorly determined at short windows: std~0.24 (ghe1,n=30) -> 0.09 (n=390,1m) -> 0.04 (n=23400,1s). Real estimator disagreement (ghe1~0.46 vs rs~0.57) explained by known biases; bias-corrected whole-session H~0.49-0.50. 1s cuts floor ~2-3x.

kill_test: control-corrected H(tau) flat at 0.5 OR coarse anti-persistence vanishes after RW control
primary_metric: control-corrected H(tau) and per-band H; 1s/1m overlap; NQ<->ES transfer
result_summary: H(tau) DECLINES with scale: micro 1-8s H=0.50 (1s OHLCV too coarse for bid-ask bounce), meso 2-30m H~0.49, coarse 30-180m H=0.462(NQ)/0.468(ES) anti-persistent after RW-control (raw 0.43 was ~40pct saturation artifact). 1s/1m meso agree to 0.003; NQ<->ES transfers. Prior micro-anti-persistence expectation NOT confirmed.
notes: Matched-length RW control subtracts structure-function saturation; distinct from anchored-at-open cone (A3)

hypothesis: Correct A1 bias calibration and cross-frequency matching
kill_test: Bias-calibrated estimators do not converge materially OR matched-date 1s/1m comparison changes the conclusion
primary_metric: inverse-calibrated H by estimator; matched-date 1s/1m gap; Rule-9a exclusions
result_summary: Executable inverse calibration gives NQ 0.473-0.499 and ES 0.466-0.485 across estimators, superseding the 0.49-0.50 claim; matched high-fill 1s/1m GHE1 is 0.490 vs 0.471 on 149 dates.

hypothesis: Add uncertainty and lag sensitivity to A2 term structure
kill_test: 95% block-bootstrap CI includes 0.5 OR coarse result is unstable across prespecified lag endpoints
primary_metric: block-bootstrap CI for corrected H; coarse-band endpoint and era sensitivity
result_summary: Coarse corrected H remains below 0.5 full-sample: NQ 0.462 CI[0.432,0.490], ES 0.468 CI[0.440,0.495]; endpoint sensitivity mostly survives but ES 45-180m and recent-era splits include 0.5, so claim is mild and era-dependent.
